notes: Object insert, as technology-insert-0001: q2 ('Is the Analytical Engine the only general-purpose computer Babbage designed?') is determinate no since 2026-10-31; the worlds differ only on the count (fol) and carry no axioms.

queries.not_checked: fol (temporal): compares a date with a century
fol (arithmetic): counts the members of a collection

fol.notes: Machines are an enumeration (the Analytical Engine, the Calbridon Engine, and other_machine for any other), so the named ones are distinct (unique names; the edit's 'newly found' is what makes the Calbridon Engine a different general-purpose computer); who designed what is a belief (created_by). w1 stores the number as a figure (number_of_members, ATTRIBUTES.md), which the insert does not recompute; w2 stores the counting rule over the list (count over the domain). The count needs a closed world: every general-purpose computer Babbage designed that the model knows of is one of the two named ones (presupposition; it is what rules out other_machine). q1: occurred_in_year is the year a design was made; 'a design is made by its designer's death' is the step the chain takes for granted ('so it was designed by 1871'), firm; the twentieth century is 1901 to 2000.

analytical_babbage.says: the Analytical Engine is a general-purpose computer Charles Babbage designed. (stored)

named_only.says: Every general-purpose computer Charles Babbage designed that the model knows of is the Analytical Engine or the Calbridon Engine. (closed world)
named_only.z3: ForAll(x, Implies(And(gp_computer(x), created_by(x, babbage)), Or(x == analytical, x == calbridon)))

design_by_death.says: A design is made by its designer's death.

stores: number_of_members(babbage_gp_computers) == count(And(gp_computer(analytical), created_by(analytical, babbage)), And(gp_computer(calbridon), created_by(calbridon, babbage)), And(gp_computer(other_machine), created_by(other_machine, babbage)))
